description: Pitch Smart daily pitch limits and required rest by age. These are the canonical youth pitching guardrails endorsed by MLB and USA Baseball. This table is the machine-readable form consumed by the practice compiler and 'Don't do this today' engine. ALWAYS verify against the live Pitch Smart page at release time and re-pin the version.

source.name: MLB / USA Baseball Pitch Smart
source.version_note: Numbers reflect the long-standing Pitch Smart age-banded daily max + required-rest framework. Cross-checked 2026-06-03 against the USA Baseball Pitch Count Recommendations PDF (7-8=50, 9-10=75, 11-12=85, 13-14=95, 15-16=95, 17-18=105 daily max). Re-verify before each release; if league rules are stricter, league rules win.

global_rules.text: If a youth pitcher pitches in the calendar days leading into a multi-day tournament, applicable rest still governs. Compiler should refuse to schedule a pitching outing that would violate accumulated rest.
All youth pitchers should take at least 4 months off competitive pitching per calendar year, with at least 2-3 of those months continuous and free of overhead throwing.
A pitcher should not pitch for multiple teams on the same calendar day.

A player should not pitch and catch in the same game beyond the pitch-count threshold that triggers required rest. Specifically: if a player catches 3 or more innings, they should not pitch that day at most youth levels.

Curveballs and other breaking pitches should not be introduced until skeletal maturity is approaching. Pitch Smart guidance: do not throw curveballs prior to roughly age 14. Fastball and change-up are the recommended pitch types for younger players.
Any pitcher reporting arm pain should stop immediately and be evaluated before returning to throwing.

Combined innings pitched in any 12-month period should not exceed Pitch Smart caps: 60 IP for ages 8 and under, 80 IP for ages 9-12, 100 IP for ages 13-14. The compiler should track rolling 12-month innings and warn as a player approaches the cap.
No pitcher should appear in a game as a pitcher for three consecutive days, regardless of pitch counts. This is a hard block independent of the daily-max and required-rest tables.

For ages 12 and under, a pitcher once removed from the mound may not return as a pitcher in the same game. For ages 13-14, a pitcher who moves to another position may return to pitch once per game. Older levels typically follow league/sanctioning-body re-entry rules.

age_tables.notes: Focus on athleticism and fun. Many programs convert this age to coach-pitch or machine-pitch; pitching is optional.

league_overrides.description: Where a sanctioning league publishes stricter pitch-count or pitch-type rules, those win. The platform must encode each league's rule set as a sibling table and apply MIN(platform_default, league_rule).

examples.note: Little League publishes its own regulation pitch-count and rest schedule; for rostered Little League players the league rule applies.
